author: @jeremyfowers

evidence.api_compatibility: No user-facing API change. The Docker image tag behavior is new (adds 'candidate' and 'candidate-v<version>' tags alongside existing 'latest' and 'edge'), and this is documented in docs/guide/install/docker.md. Existing tags are unaffected.
evidence.documentation: docs/guide/install/docker.md updated with a table describing the three rolling tags (latest, candidate, edge) and the immutable per-version tags. The change is consistent with the workflow behavior.
evidence.manual_release_testing: The new 'candidate' rolling tag behavior on release-v* branches is user-facing Docker image behavior. Prior to the next release, verify that a push to the current release-v* branch produces an image tagged 'candidate' with the correct candidate-v<version> tag and that it does not overwrite the 'latest' tag. Also confirm the scheduled release-branch-creation workflow (part of the same PR series) functions end-to-end.
evidence.post_approval_commits: One commit (2da5cc76, 'ci: parse version.py arguments with argparse') was added after the first and latest approval at 19:51:50Z (submitted at 19:59:00Z). It replaces an argv scan with argparse in tools/version.py in response to review feedback. It does not change version output, does not touch the workflow file, and stays within the PR scope; however it was merged without a renewed approval.
evidence.review: PR approved by @superm1 on 2026-09-14T19:51:50Z. @superm1 has Docker/containers listed as a subject-area expertise, so subject-matter review is satisfied. One automated comment from @chatgpt-codex-connector[bot] flagged a race condition between concurrent builds on the rolling candidate tag; no human acknowledged or addressed this comment.
evidence.security: Low risk. The workflow change adds release-v* as a trigger branch and introduces tag-naming logic; the existing docker/login-action, build-push-action, and signing pipeline are unchanged. No new secrets, credential flows, or external network calls are introduced. The workflow pushes as the GITHUB_TOKEN actor.
evidence.tests: No tests added. The change is a CI workflow modification plus documentation update; test additions would normally not be expected for this type of change, but the workflow uses an inline python3 tools/version.py call whose correctness is assumed rather than verified.

maintainer_todos.text: Verify the post-approval argparse commit (2da5cc7) does not change version.py behavior observed by the workflow and was within the spirit of the original review.
Decide whether the bot-identified race condition (concurrent release-v* pushes overwriting the rolling candidate tag) needs a fix or is an acceptable residual risk.

subject: ci: publish release branch builds to the candidate Docker tag (#3581)
summary: Publishes release-v* branch builds as a rolling 'candidate' Docker tag and an immutable 'candidate-v<version>' tag, and documents the new tag scheme.
verdict_reason: One commit (argparse refactor of tools/version.py) was added after @superm1's approval, and a bot review raised an unaddressed concern about potential stale candidate tag updates from concurrent builds.
